report.tagline: Google's email, documents, spreadsheets, video calls and storage, free for people and paid per user for businesses, now with Gemini AI built in.
report.simpleSummary: Gmail is Google's free email, and Google Workspace is the paid version for businesses. With Workspace, a company gets email on its own domain (like you@yourcompany.com), plus Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet and Calendar, all in the browser. Since January 2025, Google's Gemini AI is included: it can write emails, summarise long threads and build spreadsheets. Google raised prices a little when it added the AI, instead of charging for AI separately.

overview.whatItDoes: Google Workspace is a set of online work apps: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat and more. Everything runs in the browser and saves to the cloud, so many people can edit one file at once. Gemini AI is built into each app, and businesses pay a monthly fee per user.
howItWorks: Anyone can use Gmail, Docs and Drive free with a Google account and 15 GB of storage.
A business signs up, connects its domain, and pays per user per month.
Admins add users, set security rules and manage devices from one console.
Teams edit files together in real time and share links instead of attachments.
Gemini writes drafts in Gmail and Docs, summarises threads and takes meeting notes in Meet.
Consumers can pay for more storage and AI through Google One AI plans.
overview.valueProposition: Simple, browser-based work tools with professional email, real-time teamwork on files and AI help included, at a lower price than many rivals.

businessModel.summary: Google Workspace makes money from per-user pricing: businesses, schools and governments pay a monthly fee for each user. Free Gmail and Docs bring in billions of users who later pay for storage or bring Workspace to work. Since 2025, AI is included in the price instead of sold as a separate add-on.

revenueStreams.detail: Consumer subscriptions for more storage and Gemini.
Free Gmail keeps users in Google's ecosystem; ads in free Gmail's Promotions tab.

businessModel.pricing: Business Starter $7, Business Standard $14, Business Plus $22 per user per month on annual billing (about 20% more on flexible monthly). Enterprise custom. Free personal Gmail with 15 GB.
costDrivers: Data centres and storage for billions of users
Sales and partner commissions for enterprise
businessModel.unitEconomics: A 10-person firm on Business Standard pays about $1,680 a year. Storage and computing for them cost Google little, because it already runs huge data centres, so margin before AI is high. Gemini adds real computing cost for heavy users, which is why Google raised prices by $2 per user instead of giving AI away. Free users cost money to serve, but a small share upgrading to Google One or bringing Workspace to work pays for them. Rough estimates; Alphabet does not report Workspace profit.

howTheyGetUsers: Free Gmail, Docs and Drive used by billions

growth.moat: Moving a company's email, files and calendars is painful, so customers stay. Gmail's huge free user base feeds paid adoption. Google's own AI models and data centres let it add AI at lower cost than many rivals.

pmLessons: Bundling AI into a tool people already use daily can beat selling AI separately; Google tried a $20 add-on, then folded it into the base price.
A free product with billions of users is a huge funnel for paid plans.
Raising prices with new value works better when users can see and use the value right away.
Pushing a new feature too hard, like AI that cannot be turned off, creates backlash.

interviewQuestions.question: Google bundled Gemini into Workspace and raised prices. Was that the right call?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare add-on vs bundle: adoption, revenue, churn, competition with Copilot. Say how you'd measure it.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase Gemini usage in Gmail?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find moments of need (long threads, replies), add helpful prompts, measure weekly use and accepted suggestions.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Workspace?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly collaborating users, not seats. Break down into seats, collaboration, AI use.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you win more large enterprises from Microsoft?
interviewQuestions.hint: Target new teams, migration tools, Excel compatibility, price and AI value, security proof.

interviewQuestions.question: A user says AI in Gmail is annoying. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find which users and why, balance discovery with control, add settings, track opt-outs.
